protocol.scope: 12 new synthetic clean-up challenges, Full and Light once each; raw input reference control. No personal transcripts, speech recognition or UI insertion.
protocol.sampling: Purposive adversarial scenarios based on user preferences, not representative random sampling.
protocol.selectiveRetryPolicy: None; retain every output, fallback, error and timing.
protocol.judge: Codex model-based qualitative review; not a blinded independent human study.
protocol.referenceInterpretation: FreeFlow reference supports literal cleanup/instruction preservation; user additionally wants explicit lists and restrained Full rewriting.

rubric.factualFidelity: Hard gate: retain every final substantive claim, qualifier, restriction, name and condition; no added fact/action. Abandoned wording of explicit self-corrections is not an independent fact. Raw reference always preserves literal content.
rubric.voiceTone: 1 strongly changes emotion/register; 3 usable but loses some voice; 5 preserves deliberate emphasis, directness and mixed-language tone.
rubric.fluency: 1 hard to read; 3 intelligible with awkwardness; 5 natural punctuation/grammar, especially Chinese and code boundaries.
rubric.structure: 1 obscures relationships; 3 readable but misses expected list/paragraph structure; 5 desired scanability with clear condition scope and no forced narrative list.
rubric.restraint: 1 executes/invents/sanitizes; 3 unnecessary paraphrase; 5 only justified cleanup, preserving clear phrasing.
rubric.preference: Fidelity-failing alternatives cannot win. Among passing alternatives choose the most readable output consistent with the users conservative rewrite/tone/list preferences; ties allowed and justified. A raw win is valid.

cases.input: Hi Maya, um, I wanted to give you the actual picture before the demo tomorrow because I think the note in the channel sounded more confident than we are. The installer is ready on my machine, and the microphone test passed on two laptops, but we have not tested the old Intel machine yet, so please don't say every Mac is covered. The thing about the dictionary, I mean the important part, is that the existing entries survived the upgrade; we didn't add a new dictionary or replace anyone's words. For the demo there are three checks I still want: open the app from a fresh download without touching the security settings, dictate a short message into the browser and make sure it lands in the selected field, and dictate a longer message while switching desktops to see whether the small recording bar stays visible. If any of those fails, record which check failed and what the person saw, but don't keep retrying until we have a pretty result. I also need to be clear about the update: the download link exists, but that doesn't prove the automatic update completed, and I don't want that distinction lost. We can still do the demo if the manual install works, as long as we call the automatic update unverified. Actually, one more thing: don't use a customer's real recording in the demo. A made-up shopping list is enough. I'm not trying to hold up the release for perfect wording; I just want the claims to match what we actually checked. Thanks.
acceptanceCriteria: Readable email with spoken greeting and closing, logical paragraphs, and three distinct demo-check items.
Preserve every qualification: tested machine counts, Intel untested, dictionary survived rather than recreated.
Fresh download without security changes; browser selected-field insert; long desktop-switch recording bar.
Failure record versus selective retries, existing link versus unverified automatic update, manual-install demo allowance.
No customer audio; synthetic shopping list; claims must match checks; no invented promise or blanket release blocker.
